Closes #474.

## Why

#179 (PR #438) checks `FALLBACK_MODEL_ID` against the model allowlist and prints it in the `api.model` startup line, but never hands it to the engine. HAL Engine fails over only through `fallbackProviders`, and `buildEngine` passed none: its `resilience` setting is a retry policy, not the fallback field #179's text assumed. So a configured fallback was never tried, the startup line and the README promised a failover that could not happen, and #434's `onFailover` hook could never fire.

# Fallback Model Allowlist

The provider block hands HAL Engine the resolved fallback as the only entry of `fallbackProviders`, the one setting HAL Engine fails over through, and an empty list while `FALLBACK_MODEL_ID` is unset, so the fallback the `api.model` line names is the one HAL Engine tries when the primary is unavailable. (#474) ([validated by `hands HAL Engine the mock and an empty fallbackProviders list when FALLBACK_MODEL_ID is unset`](../../apps/api/test/server.test.ts#L171), [validated by `hands HAL Engine the mock fallback as the only fallbackProviders entry when FALLBACK_MODEL_ID is mock`](../../apps/api/test/server.test.ts#L178))

- [ ] Startup logs include safe fallback model details.
- [ ] The HAL Engine is initialized with the correctly resolved fallback provider.
- [ ] The application refuses non-mock fallback models until a vendor is officially chosen.
- [ ] The mock model is refused as a fallback when the primary model is real.

Its `resilience` setting is a retry policy and has no fallback field. Before the fix in issue #474 and PR #475, `buildEngine` in apps/api/src/server.ts passed `createHalEngine` a `provider` and no `fallbackProviders`. The fallback was checked against the allowlist and named in the `api.model` startup line, but it was never tried. The fix passes the resolved fallback as the only entry of `fallbackProviders`, or an empty list when FALLBACK_MODEL_ID is unset. Only the mock row can currently be a fallback, because a real fallback needs a chosen vendor (KU-07).
